headline: I Was Given Three Seconds To Speak In Parliament And Used Them To Announce My Lunch Order
body:
I didn't choose the three-second speaking life; the three-second speaking life chose me. When the Speaker finally looked in my direction, I knew I had exactly enough time to either address the crumbling infrastructure of my constituency or ensure that my canteen order arrived before the afternoon session began. Given that the parliamentary process moves with the same urgency as a sloth on a holiday, I chose the only logical path: I leaned into the mic and shouted, 'One extra-spicy paneer roll, no onions, delivery to Seat 402.'

It was a moment of pure, unadulterated legislative efficiency. My colleagues across the aisle were baffled, but honestly, have you ever tried to secure a decent lunch in this building without a formal notice period? I figured that if I’m only allowed to participate in democracy for the time it takes to sneeze, I might as well use that energy to avoid starvation. The look on the Parliamentary staff's face when they frantically scrambled to locate a delivery boy in the central hall was worth more than any speech on fiscal policy I could have cobbled together.

I’ve been told that my intervention will be struck from the official record, but the canteen manager has already promised my paneer roll will be prioritized. If the House is going to treat our voices as mere background noise, I might as well turn that noise into a culinary transaction. Tomorrow, if they give me four seconds, I’m going to try to order a side of fries, provided the microphone doesn't get cut off mid-ketchup.
caption: When the mic time is shorter than a reel, you gotta make the order count. Parliament canteen staff, you've been warned. #ParliamentDiaries #LegislativeHunger #DemocracyLunch #DelhiLife (satire)
igHook: What would you order if you only had 3 seconds of airtime in the Lok Sabha?
imagePrompt: A blurry, low-angle shot of a polished wooden microphone stand inside a dimly lit legislative chamber with ornate pillars and red carpet in the background.

sourceHeadline.title: Union Minister and NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi says SC/ST MPs not given enough time to speak in Parliament

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 manages the best balance of absurdity and specificity. By choosing a mundane, high-stakes 'paneer roll' order as the sole use of limited legislative time, it creates a vivid image and a relatable human reaction to bureaucratic absurdity, avoiding the repetitive 'time-limit' tropes seen in the other candidates.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article is a harmless, satirical piece about parliamentary procedure and the absurdity of limited speaking time. It does not name any real individuals, target protected groups, or make defamatory claims, and the image prompt is generic and descriptive.
